headline: Aspinall hits 170 finish to beat Clemens 10-7
standfirst: Nathan Aspinall averaged 100.72 and took out a 170 checkout on his way past Gabriel Clemens into the Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals.
body: Nathan Aspinall reached the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam of Darts on Thursday evening, beating Gabriel Clemens 10-7 in the last 16 at Wolverhampton. Aspinall averaged 100.72 to the German’s 96.55 and broke throw five times to Clemens’s three.

He made the better start, taking the opening two legs, the second in 11 darts, before Clemens won three in a row to lead 3-2. Aspinall levelled, then took the next two to go 5-3 up, and the match looked to be heading his way.

Clemens was not done. He won three of the next four legs, including a break of throw, to move 6-5 ahead, and he hit ten 180s to Aspinall’s seven. But the heavy scoring did not translate into finishing: Clemens converted 31.82 per cent of his checkout chances, against 52.63 for Aspinall.

That gap decided the closing stretch. Aspinall levelled at 6-6, broke again for 7-6 and then won leg 15 in 12 darts with a 170 checkout, the biggest finish of the night, to lead 9-6. Clemens pulled one back on the Aspinall throw, but Aspinall broke once more in 13 darts to seal the win.
Aspinall now meets Gian van Veen in the quarter-finals on Saturday evening.
